verses.text: The oracle of God which Habak'kuk the prophet saw.
O LORD, how long shall I cry for help,
Why do you make me see wrongs
So the law is slacked
Look among the nations, and see;
For behold, I am rousing the Chalde'ans,
Dread and fearsome are they;
Their horses are swifter than leopards,
They all come for violence;
At kings they scoff,
Then they sweep by like the wind and go on,
Are you not from everlasting,
You who are of purer eyes than to behold evil
For you make men like the fish of the sea,
He brings all of them up with a hook,
Therefore he sacrifices to his net
Is he then to keep on emptying his net,
I will take my stand to watch,
And the LORD answered me:
For still the vision awaits its time;
Behold, he whose soul is not upright in him shall fail,
Moreover, wine is treacherous;
Shall not all these take up their taunt against him, in scoffing derision of him, and say,
Will not your debtors suddenly arise,
Because you have plundered many nations,
Woe to him who gets evil gain for his house,
You have devised shame to your house
For the stone will cry out from the wall,
Woe to him who builds a town with blood,
Behold, is it not from the LORD of hosts
For the earth will be filled
Woe to him who makes his neighbors drink
You will be sated with contempt instead of glory.
The violence done to Lebanon will overwhelm you;
What profit is an idol
Woe to him who says to a wooden thing, Awake;
But the LORD is in his holy temple;
A prayer of Habak'kuk the prophet, accord- ing to Shigion'oth.
O LORD, I have heard the report of you,
God came from Te'man,
His brightness was like the light,
Before him went pestilence,
He stood and measured the earth;
I saw the tents of Cush'an in affliction;
Was your wrath against the rivers, O LORD?
You stripped the sheath from your bow,
The mountains saw you, and writhed;
The sun and moon stood still in their habitation
You bestrode the earth in fury,
You went forth for the salvation of your people,
You pierced with your shafts the head of his warriors,
You trampled the sea with your horses,
I hear, and my body trembles,
Though the fig tree does not blossom,
yet I will rejoice in the LORD,
GOD, the Lord, is my strength;
